title: [Smartswitch] Bug: The DPU auto rebooting expectation in the NPU memory exhaustion/kernel panic is not correct for SN4280
author: congh-nvidia
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

There was a new DPU uptime validation added to the NPU memory exhaustion/kernel panic test cases by PR https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/24136.
I the test cases test_dpu_status_post_switch_mem_exhaustion and test_dpu_status_post_switch_kernel_panic, it expects the DPU are rebooted along with the NPU.

But this expectation is not correct for SN4280. The actual behavior is, when the NPU is rebooted due to memory exhaustion or kernel panic, the DPUs are not rebooted automatically.

Test failure:
```
RuntimeError: Thread worker aborted: DPU DPU0 did not reboot: boot time is unchanged
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the test case test_dpu_status_post_switch_kernel_panic on SN4280 testbed.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

This validation should be skipped on SN4280 in test_dpu_status_post_switch_kernel_panic and test_dpu_status_post_switch_mem_exhaustion.


linkedPullRequests.title: Fix SN4280 DPU reboot expectation after NPU crash
linkedPullRequests.author: xwjiang-ms
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR
Fix SN4280 SmartSwitch NPU crash tests so they do not assert that DPUs reboot during NPU memory exhaustion/kernel panic recovery.

SN4280 keeps DPUs up when the NPU recovers from these crash scenarios. The tests should still verify DPU operational status and connectivity after recovery, but the optional uptime-based reboot validation is not valid for this platform.

Fixes sonic-net/sonic-mgmt#26455

### Type of change
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement

### Back port request
- [ ] 202205
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [x] 202605

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
Nightly test `test_dpu_status_post_switch_kernel_panic` fails on SN4280 with `DPU DPU0 did not reboot: boot time is unchanged`. This is expected platform behavior for SN4280 NPU crash recovery, not a DPU recovery failure.

#### How did you do it?
Added a small platform expectation helper and used it to disable the optional DPU uptime reboot validation only for SN4280 in the NPU memory exhaustion and NPU kernel panic tests.

#### How did you verify/test it?
- Ran `python -m py_compile tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/test_reload_dpu.py`
- Ran `git diff --check`

#### Any platform specific information?
Mellanox-SN4280 keeps DPUs up during NPU memory exhaustion/kernel panic recovery.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?
N/A

comments.author: xwjiang-ms
comments.body:
<!-- sonic-my-pr-review:v1 sha=1285c636f35a966981e221242223554b3e3a1456 at=2026-08-09T23:08:15Z -->
## AI review — risk: LOW

**Verified**
- The fix addresses exactly the linked issue. #26455 names both `test_dpu_status_post_switch_mem_exhaustion` and `test_dpu_status_post_switch_kernel_panic` and the DPU uptime validation added by PR #24136, with failure `DPU DPU0 did not reboot: boot time is unchanged`. This PR gates `pre_boot_times` in exactly those two tests (`tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/test_reload_dpu.py:171`, `:221`).
- `pre_boot_times=None` disables *only* the uptime reboot check. Traced into `post_test_dpu_check` (`tests/smartswitch/common/device_utils_dpu.py:781`): `if pre_boot_times and dpu_name in pre_boot_times:` guards the `"...did not reboot: boot time is unchanged"` assertion (`:785`). With `None`, the DPU-online check (`:754`), critical-process check (`:764`), reboot-cause check (`:771`) and post-check ping (`:812`) all still run — matching the PR's claim that operational status and connectivity are still verified.
- Blast radius is correctly narrow. `expects_dpu_reboot_after_npu_crash` returns `False` only when `duthost.facts['hwsku']` starts with `Mellanox-SN4280`; every other platform still records `pre_boot_times` and enforces the reboot assertion unchanged. The four other tests in this file that expect a real DPU reboot (`:100`, `:283`, `:353`, `:416`, `:465`) are untouched.
- `hwsku.startswith("Mellanox-SN4280")` matches the reported `Mellanox-SN4280-O28`.
- `py_compile` of the head revision passes.

### Worth addressing
1. **(Low) `reboot_cause` check still runs on SN4280** — `tests/smartswitch/common/device_utils_dpu.py:771`. `post_test_dpus_check` is still called with `re.compile(r"reboot|Non-Hardware", re.IGNORECASE)`, so the DPU reboot-cause assertion executes even when the DPU is expected *not* to reboot. This is fine given the issue's observed failure was the uptime assertion (which runs after and would only be reached if the reboot-cause check passed), but if a future SN4280 image reports a reboot-cause that no longer matches this regex on a non-rebooting DPU, that assertion — not the now-disabled uptime one — would fail. Not blocking; just flagging that the reboot-cause expectation was left in place while the reboot uptime expectation was removed.

### Nits
- New branch can't be unit-tested (needs SmartSwitch hardware); verification was `py_compile`/`git diff --check` only, which is acceptable for a platform-gated skip.
- Back-port marked 202605 only, consistent with where PR #24136 (the regression source) landed.

No blocking issues. The change is correctly scoped to the two NPU-crash tests and the single platform, and keeps all non-reboot health checks intact.
